payload.text:
Where a defect in the artifact makes a gate unprovable, the harness NAMES it and counts the slide ungradeable rather than passing it. Measured 2026-09-09: the token add("Producer", REEL.producer || "Snorkeltoast") in player.html means blanking producer swaps a configured value for a literal rather than removing the row, so the presence control can never reach an empty render for a session crawl. CITED BY TOKEN AND NOT BY LINE, which is the correction: this row carried a line number until 2026-09-09 and 3903937 moved it. The dead number is deliberately not restated: to any scanner it is indistinguishable from a live one, which is the property that made the error invisible. Slide 1's presence figure of 28.34 PASSED the gate for the wrong reason -- both frames lack the session details and differ elsewhere. That 28.34 predates the crawl fix and FLOORS.md now reports 53.432 for the same slide; both are real, from different runs, and neither changes this row's point, but a reader reconciling them without this sentence could not. Session crawls therefore report presence UNPROVABLE with the player token as the reason, and when the literal goes the gate becomes sound with no harness change. AC-3.7 IS WITHDRAWN (hv, yak-shaving) SO THIS ROW'S INSTANCE IS PERMANENT, WHICH STRENGTHENS IT RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. The producer literal is not going to be gated on, so slide 1 stays presence UNPROVABLE unless cc happens to drop the fallback at the template pull -- optional and ungated. That is exactly the situation this row exists for: a gate the artifact makes unprovable is NAMED and the slide is counted ungradeable, permanently, rather than passed. The reel reads 21 of 22 and says why.
THIS ROW SAYS "WHEN THE LITERAL GOES THE GATE BECOMES SOUND WITH NO HARNESS CHANGE", AND THAT SENTENCE IS NOW FALSE. Measured by vc 2026-09-10 08:27Z. The row also predicted the trigger -- "unless cc happens to drop the fallback at the template pull, optional and ungated" -- and **cc HAS dropped it**, so the prediction fired and the consequence recorded beside it does not hold.
WHAT WAS MEASURED, THREE READS ACROSS TWO FILES. `add` is identical in both players and SKIPS FALSY: `const add = (k, v) => { if (v) rows.push(...) }` at `player.html:624`. The reference is `add("Producer", REEL.producer || "Snorkeltoast")` at `:628`; **cc's pull is `add("Producer", REEL.producer)` at `:629`.** So blanking `producer` gives the reference a truthy `"Snorkeltoast"` and the row survives stripping, while cc's gives `""`, which `add` skips -- **the row vanishes and the presence control reaches an empty render.** The gate IS sound on a Rust-built artifact.
**BUT THE HARNESS CANNOT SEE THAT, WHICH IS WHY A HARNESS CHANGE IS REQUIRED AFTER ALL.** `strip_reason(slide)` returns `UNSTRIPPABLE.get((slide.get("kind"), slide.get("crawl")))` -- **keyed on the SLIDE'S KIND and nothing else.** It takes no artifact and reads no player. So on cc's artifact, where the crawl strips perfectly, it will still return the reason and the slide will still be counted ungradeable: **a FALSE ungradeable, which silently removes from grading a slide that could have been graded.**
**THE ROW'S PROPERTY SURVIVES AND THE FORWARD-LOOKING CLAUSE DOES NOT**, which is the AC-3.8 split: "where a defect in the artifact makes a gate unprovable, the harness NAMES it and counts the slide ungradeable" is true and demonstrated on the reference. What is false is the prediction about what happens when the defect goes. Not reopened; corrected, because a satisfied row carrying a false sentence is worse than an open one.
**AND IT IS THE `limits` SHAPE ONE TABLE ALONG** -- the same defect snorkeltoast corrected on AC-3.6 this morning. A rule FIXED IN ADVANCE about what a player does, where the sound form is answerable from the ARTIFACT ALONE. `strip_reason` should ask whether THIS artifact's player supplies a literal the payload cannot remove, greppable from the file the way `stamp_fault` reads the tag. Then it is right for both implementations and stays right when either player changes.
**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ONE-SHOT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS RECORDED BEFORE THE BUILD AND NOT AFTER:** FLOORS.md reports 22 gradeable of 23 with slide 1 the single refusal. cc's artifact should give 23 of 23. **The first compare will therefore show a GRADEABILITY DIFFERENCE between ref and new, and it is the port REMOVING a defect** -- the hardest kind to read correctly in the moment. It belongs in `PORT_EXPECTATIONS` beforehand; snorkeltoast has it. **vc has NOT run this**: it is a source reading of two files and one function, testable the moment cc's artifact exists.
AND cc'S MODULE DOC UNDERSTATES WHAT THAT LINE BUYS: `template.rs` records the divergence as H3 only -- keeping a brand literal out of the binary. The same removal makes the session crawl strippable, which the reference cannot do and which `showreel-harness:1070` records as a defect "not the harness's to make". **cc fixed it while solving something else and neither side knew.**
